problem: In Multi-Object Navigation, RL agents must learn mapping and spatial reasoning from sparse reward alone, which is inefficient and leaves memory poorly spatially structured, even for agents with explicit neural maps.
motivation: Multi-ON needs the agent to remember where earlier-seen objects are and retrieve them later, so mapping and spatial reasoning matter. Inspired by human spatial-navigation studies (sense of direction, relative distance judgement), the authors hypothesise that supervising the agent to localise already-seen targets will shape better internal representations.
key_idea: Add auxiliary classification losses on the GRU hidden state that predict whether the current target was already observed, and if so its relative direction and distance, to encourage emergent mapping in RL-trained agents.
insight: Direction and distance supervision are strong and complementary (ProjNeuralMap val Success 21.8 -> 40.2 with direction, -> 44.3 with distance, -> 49.2 with the observed-target loss). The gains hold with and without spatial inductive bias (NoMap 16.7 -> 43.0 test Success), so much of the map structure can be learned from supervision. Linear probes show the auxiliary-trained agent's GRU state encodes more direction/distance/observed-target information.
method: Base agents (from MultiON): RGB-D CNN + target-class and previous-action embeddings, GRU, actor-critic heads, trained with PPO; variants NoMap, ProjNeuralMap (projective neural map with max-pool write), OracleMap, OracleEgoMap
Direction auxiliary task: classify the angle (12 bins of 30°) from agent to the target object, only when the target has been seen, with GT taken from the egocentric oracle map
Distance auxiliary task: classify the Euclidean distance on the egocentric 50x50 map (36 bins, 1 unit each) to the seen target
Observed-target auxiliary task: binary prediction of whether the current target has ever been in the field of view

Heads and loss: each head is a single linear layer + softmax on the GRU hidden state, trained with cross-entropy, Ltot = L_PPO + 0.25 (L_dir + L_dist + L_obs); heads are used at training only, not at inference
Challenge entry: ProjNeuralMap trained 80M steps with the aux losses, then finetuned 20M steps with vanilla RL only

setting.backbone: CNN + GRU actor-critic (ProjNeuralMap, NoMap; also OracleEgoMap) trained from scratch with PPO
setting.training_data: Multi-ON 3-ON episodes on Matterport3D: 61 train scenes, 50,000 episodes per scene; 70M RL steps (80M+20M for the challenge entry)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 256x256 + target object class one-hot + previous action; odometry/perfect localization assumed
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: move forward 0.25 m, turn left 30°, turn right 30°, found
setting.privileged: Auxiliary labels (GT object positions, explored area, agent pose) are used during training only; at test time perfect localization/odometry is assumed, and no oracle maps for the proposed agents (Oracle baselines are marked incomparable)

numbers_note: Multi-ON is not in the canonical list, so results are tagged 'other'. A last-minute bug note says corrected Table III values would be 52.3, 65.9, 36.4, 45.7 (presumably for ProjNeuralMap with aux losses).
results: Auxiliary losses roughly double ProjNeuralMap success on test (25.9 -> 57.7) and lift NoMap from 16.7 to 43.0. ProjNeuralMap with aux losses matches the oracle OracleMap on Success and Progress, and beats OracleEgoMap. The entry won the CVPR 2021 Multi-ON challenge (Test-Standard PPL 45 vs SGoLAM 39 and VIMP 36).
limitations: Auxiliary supervision needs privileged simulator information (GT object positions, explored area) during training
Evaluated only on 3-ON with coloured cylinders in simulation, assuming perfect localization; no real-robot tests

A bug in the official Multi-ON code leaked extra information to OracleEgoMap and affected training supervision; results are slightly changed, and test results use 1,000-episode subsets with high variance
